sources.quote: Taloid Talu, Lavu (Chen 2010); Kuansi (Castro, Flaming & Crook 2010); Naruo (Foley 2020); Tagu (Yang, et al. 2017); [...] PN PCN Lisoid Loloid Laloid Taloid Lahoid Sanoid *1 high, modal 33/44 33 55 55 33/21 33~44/21 *2 low, breathy 55/21 55/21 55/21 21~31 53/31~21 33~55/21 *3 mid, creaky 33~44 33 33 33 33 33 *H mid, tense 33~44/35 33 33 33~44 54~33/35 33~44 *L low, tense 55/21 55/21 21 21~31 21~31/35 55/21 [...] (3) PN tone correspondences in six proposed clusters of CN. / = split; ~ = within-cluster variation
sources.locator: single-page poster: panel 3 'Method', table (1) (languages and sources) and panel 4 'Results', table (3) (PN tone correspondences by cluster; Taloid = 4th value column after the PCN label)
sources.note: Applies Dockum's Tonal Comparative Method to ~130 cognate sets from 23 Ngwi languages; for the Taloid cluster (Talu, Lavu, Tagu, Kuansi, Naruo) Proto-Ngwi *1 > 55, *2 > 21~31, *3 > 33, *H > 33~44, *L > 21~31, i.e. Talu/Lavu operate with high-level 55, mid 33(~44) and low-falling 21~31 categories; argues the proposed Central-Ngwi tone splits are cluster-level, not Proto-Central-Ngwi.
sources.venue: Poster presented at the Annual Meeting of the Linguistic Society of America, Washington, DC
